svg.text: Beyond chat use cases: where they belong and what solves them best
Each cell names the ideal solution and the use cases it fits. Solutions and their trade-offs: see 08-extending-matrix.svg.
Highlighted: use cases solved with Iframe + Widget API.
Others may see something different or nothing.
Same experience for anyone in one Matrix room
Only the room guarantees that every member sees the same thing.
Send enhanced / rich messages (e.g. auto-populated weather data)
Calendar view from an external service
hybrid: Matrix for membership + MatrixRTC, own server for the rest
UI for bots and external services
6 are personal: build them into the client
Almost all of them fit best as native client features or modules. Their
functionality does not rely on every room member having access to them, so they need
neither support in all clients nor a cross-client widget.
29 are room features: 10 of them on Iframe + Widget API
Another 17 (polls, lists, forms, renderers, bot workflows, ...) use A2UI or a bot,
but can be built on Iframe + Widget API too. 2 (calendar events, time zone resolver)
are best built into the client.
Topics that need a decision beyond picking one of the solutions above.
How much control over the layout of beyond-chat content should the client
developer own, and how much the Matrix spec? Example: cross-client layout
sharing, where a moderator sets a layout (timeline in the centre, widget X
left, widget Y right) and users opt in.
How do users find and add widgets (widget browser, Modular integration
manager)? The one case where a client-wide widget makes sense, but it is
tricky security-wise, so a custom client may fit best. Long term: a
specced discovery format that clients support. Room widgets are an easy
All-client implementation of event composer extensions
Examples: send enhanced / rich messages, such as auto-populated weather
data; create new calendar events from the composer. Does this need a spec,
or is a native client implementation without a shared approach enough? A
bot can do it by enhancing the input: the bot fetches the weather and
replies to the message (or adds a custom A2UI edit rendering).
